subject: EU-only data partitioning and escrow plan for regulated pilot
messages:
From: Alice Berg <alice.berg@eurohealth.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@eurohealth.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:15:00 +0100
Subject: EU-only processing & escrow — pilot questions

Hi Jasmine,

We’re kicking off a small regulated pilot and need to confirm a few things up front about data residency and controls. High level: EuroHealth requires that all patient-derived inputs and model inference outputs remain physically in the EU, and that backups and logs do not leave the EU. We’re evaluating options and would like to understand Redwood’s ability to commit to: 

- EU-only processing (no replication outside of EU regions) in contract and technical enforcement
- VPC peering / Private Connect so our traffic does not traverse the public internet
- Customer-managed key escrow or an HSM operated by a EU-based KMS provider (we can discuss acceptable providers)
- Evidence artifacts: SIG/CAIQ summary, SOC 2 report, and any DPIA guidance you can share

Can you also confirm whether you can offer physical partitioning (dedicated pool) for this pilot versus logical/tenant isolation only? We’d like to see how quick a pilot deploy could be and what the MAP would look like.

Attaching a short DPIA request form. Happy to join a quick call this week.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Berg
Head of Security & Privacy
EuroHealth Systems GmbH

Attachment: request-dpia-eurohealth.pdf (1 page)
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Alice Berg <alice.berg@eurohealth.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 12:03:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: EU-only processing & escrow — pilot questions

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear note and the DPIA template. Short answer up front: yes, we can support an EU-only processing commitment for a regulated pilot, and we have three implementation patterns we commonly propose depending on risk tolerance and operational constraints. I’ve summarized the options at a high level below and attached a short options brief.

1) Hosted regional + Private Connect (fastest): hosted API pinned to an EU region with strict routing policy + Private Connect peering to keep traffic on private paths. Logical tenant isolation, data persistency restricted to EU-backed storage. Good for quick pilots but shared runtime.

2) Dedicated capacity (recommended for regulated pilots): reserved GPU pools physically isolated by customer, with per-customer VPC peering and optional regional HSM/KMS integration. We can commit contractually to not replicate data out of EU for this deployment.

3) Private deployment (on-prem/VPC appliance): customer-managed installation (air-gapped option available) — full control but longer lead time.

Questions to help us scope the MAP:
- Do you require contract language that explicitly prohibits backups leaving the EU, or will a technical control + audit evidence suffice?
- Is customer-managed KMS mandatory, or is holding an escrowed key in an EU HSM acceptable?
- Any minimum retention windows for logs/trace you need to enforce?

We can do a 30–45 minute technical + legal sync. Proposed MAP (high level):
- Week 0: Confirm architecture choice + sign pilot SOW addendum
- Week 1–2: Provision dedicated pool / Private Connect config + legal review
- Week 3: Test keys & data residency validation; sample DPIA notes
- Week 4: Pilot go-live (limited traffic) and evidence delivery (SIG summary, SOC 2 pages)

I’ve attached the brief: redwood-eu-processing-options.pdf. Naomi — copying you for contract language and SCCs guidance.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-eu-processing-options.pdf (3 pages)
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Alice Berg <alice.berg@eurohealth.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 10:22:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: EU-only processing & escrow — pilot questions

Hi Alice,

Thanks for raising these items. A few legal/contract points to note: 

- We can include a bespoke clause in the pilot SOW/DPA that states: "Redwood will process Customer Data in EU-only regions and will not transfer such data outside the EU for the duration of the pilot." We’ll also include the standard SCCs as an addendum where applicable.
- Regarding key custody: we can offer two options — customer-managed keys via customer KMS tenant (preferred) or Redwood-maintained keys with escrow stored in an EU-based HSM managed by our KMS partner. If escrowed, we will provide dual-control access logs and quarterly attestations.
- For evidence: we will provide our latest SIG self-assessment summary (high-level) and an excerpt of our SOC 2 scope relevant to hosting/regional processing. Full SOC 2 report available under NDA.

I’m attaching a short summary (redwood-sig-summary.xlsx) with the sections we commonly hand to customers for initial review. If EuroHealth has any specific contractual redlines (e.g., explicit prohibition on cross-border backups), please send them and we’ll flag whether they’re feasible during a pilot.

Happy to join the call — Jasmine, can you propose two times?

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-sig-summary.xlsx (2 sheets)
From: Alice Berg <alice.berg@eurohealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 08:47:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: EU-only processing & escrow — pilot questions

Thanks Naomi/Jasmine — that all looks reasonable. A couple clarifications from EuroHealth legal/security: 

- We prefer customer-managed keys in our KMS tenant, but will accept an escrowed EU-HSM if Redwood can demonstrate dual-control and auditable release procedures.
- Backups: must remain in EU. If there is any short-term replication for DR, it must be to an EU-only DR region; cross-border DR is not acceptable for our pilot.
- We’ll want a short DPIA note from Redwood describing residual risk for model inference (we’ll attach our DPIA template filled in as a baseline).

Proposed call times: Thu 25 Mar 2027 09:00 CET or Thu 25 Mar 2027 15:00 CET. Please confirm.

Regards,
Alice

Hi Alice — thanks, can confirm on the technical side: 

- Dedicated capacity: we can provision a reserved GPU pool in an EU data center with strict tenancy mapping. Data stores and snapshots will be configured to use EU-only storage endpoints; we will block egress rules at the subnet level to prevent accidental routing outside the EU.
- Private Connect: we support partner Private Connect (cloud-provider-specific) and can give you a list of required prefixes and peering ACLs for the initial setup.
- KMS/HSM: customer-managed KMS is supported via Bring Your Own Key; we can also do an escrow workflow where Redwood stores an encrypted key in an EU HSM and provides dual-control release logs.
- DPIA input: we’ll produce a short companion note (1–2 pages) outlining residual inference risks and mitigations for the pilot.

I’ve added a draft MAP spreadsheet and a technical checklist to the Drive link (see related_links). Proposed next step: sign pilot addendum and target provisioning start on 29 Mar 2027.

Cheers,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
